verdict.text: Private and beta apps require no review and can be used immediately within an account, but public and unlisted apps require a formal multi-stage review covering submission completeness, branding, functionality, usability, compliance, and security testing against OWASP Top 10 risks.
verdict.label: Sourced
verdict.quote: Private and beta apps do not require review.

hands_on_time.label: Inferred
hands_on_time.note: Creating the app in the Marketplace build flow, setting up credentials, configuring redirect URIs, and picking granular scopes takes under 30 minutes for a standard setup.

waiting_time.label: Sourced
waiting_time.quote: An app's review time varies based on app quality, usability, quantity and function of features, and clarity of information (descriptions, images, videos).

prerequisites.text: Account administrator role or role permissions granting 'View' and 'Edit' for 'Zoom for developers' in the Zoom web portal under User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced Features.
prerequisites.label: Sourced
prerequisites.quote: In the Zoom web portal, the administrator must go to User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced Features and select the View

prerequisites.text: An account admin or user with Marketplace permissions must pre-approve the app to enable it for end-users.
prerequisites.label: Sourced
prerequisites.quote: To enable apps for end-users, an account admin, or user with Marketplace permissions for their Zoom Account, must pre-approve the app.

prerequisites.text: For public or unlisted marketplace apps, comprehensive technical design documentation outlining architecture, security controls, and data handling is required.
prerequisites.label: Sourced
prerequisites.quote: As part of the app submission process, all developers must complete the Technical Design section of the build flow.

setup_steps.text: Log in to the Zoom Marketplace and create a new application using the build flow.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Create a new application in the Zoom Marketplace.

setup_steps.text: Configure basic information and set your OAuth Redirect URL (or loopback URI like http://127.0.0.1:port/callback for PKCE/native clients) in your Marketplace app configuration.
setup_steps.label: Inferred
setup_steps.note: Derived from the Zoom OAuth redirect URI instructions and loopback URI specifications in the OAuth documentation.

setup_steps.text: If building a native or public client without a backend secret, navigate to App Credentials under Basic Information and toggle 'Use Public Client OAuth' to on.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Open your app and navigate to App Credentials under Basic Information. Toggle Use Public Client OAuth to on.

setup_steps.text: Navigate to Scopes, click 'Add Scopes', and select the granular scopes required for your integration.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Under Scopes, click Add Scopes. Select the granular scopes you'd like to use in the app.

setup_steps.text: Mark non-essential granular scopes as 'Optional' so that users can authorize minimal permissions initially.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: In that list, you can mark a scope Optional. Scopes not marked as optional will be required when using the basic authorization query.

setup_steps.text: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret from App Credentials (and paste them into your integration platform or Composio custom auth config if applicable).
setup_steps.label: Inferred
setup_steps.note: Standard procedure for confidential OAuth clients to obtain credentials from the App Credentials screen.

setup_steps.text: Test your app locally by going to the Local Test page and selecting 'Add App Now' to obtain user authorization within your account.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: To do this, navigate to the Local Test page, and choose Add App Now.

setup_steps.text: If publishing publicly or unlisted, complete the submission forms (including technical design, branding, and compliance) and submit for App Marketplace review.
setup_steps.label: Inferred
setup_steps.note: Inferred from the review submission instructions detailed in the app review documentation.

limits_before_approval.text: Private and beta apps are exempt from marketplace review and can be shared and used internally without submitting for review.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: Private and beta apps do not require review.

limits_before_approval.text: Access tokens expire after 1 hour (3600 seconds) and must be refreshed.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: Access tokens expire after one hour. After your access token expires, you can follow the refresh flow to get a new one.

limits_before_approval.text: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days, requiring users to re-authenticate if inactive.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days. You should always use the latest refresh token for the next refresh request.

limits_before_approval.text: Non-admin end-users cannot install or use apps until an account admin pre-approves the app.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: To enable apps for end-users, an account admin, or user with Marketplace permissions for their Zoom Account, must pre-approve the app.

limits_before_approval.text: Production apps must implement a deauthorization notification endpoint URL to handle user data deletion upon app uninstall.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: The request goes to the deauthorization notification endpoint URL you specified on the App Listing page.

approval_process.text: Submission completeness & branding review: Zoom verifies minimal submission criteria, metadata, technical design documentation, and adherence to Zoom branding guidelines.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: We verify that your app meets the minimal criteria required to be accepted into our review process.

approval_process.text: Functionality & usability review: The review team tests installation, uninstallation, configuration settings, user sign-up, and real data flow.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: We review your app's functionality and confirm that it works as you described.

approval_process.text: Scope evaluation: The Marketplace Security Review Team verifies that the app only requests the minimum necessary OAuth scopes required for its functionality.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: The Marketplace Security Review Team verifies that the app only requests the minimum necessary OAuth scopes required for its functionality.

approval_process.text: Security testing: Apps undergo automated web scanning, least-privilege verification, library vulnerability checks, and manual assessments against OWASP Top 10 risks.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: Apps are tested against the OWASP Top 10 risks and undergo a variety of assessments, including: Verification of least-privilege access. Web application security scanning.

approval_process.text: Remediation & re-submission: Zoom provides a report explaining reasons for rejection and action items to fix before resubmitting.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: We provide a report explaining the reasons we did not accept the app and action items you can complete to remediate the issues.

approval_process.text: Ongoing monitoring: Zoom continuously monitors published apps and may request remediation or suspend apps that pose significant risks.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: We monitor applications that have passed app review and been published to the App Marketplace to ensure continued compliance with our guidelines.

likely_blockers.text: Requesting excessive or unjustified scopes beyond the minimal requirements of the integration.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: The Marketplace Security Review Team verifies that the app only requests the minimum necessary OAuth scopes required for its functionality.

likely_blockers.text: Security vulnerabilities or failing OWASP Top 10 assessments during technical security scanning.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: Apps are tested against the OWASP Top 10 risks and undergo a variety of assessments, including: Verification of least-privilege access. Web application security scanning.

likely_blockers.text: Presenting ads to users or collecting user data for marketing purposes, which violates usability policies.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: Your app should not present advertising to Zoom users or collect user information for marketing purposes.

likely_blockers.text: Incomplete technical design documentation or unclear test plans and listing descriptions.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: Apps with poorly described scopes, confusing UI, or unclear listing information may require a lengthy review process.

likely_blockers.text: Violating Zoom branding guidelines or intellectual property rules in the app name, description, or assets.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: Zoom reserves the right to remove or require a revision to any content, in whole or part, including an app name, that violates: Zoom's

likely_blockers.text: Missing account administrator permissions or pre-approval in the Zoom organization.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: To enable apps for end-users, an account admin, or user with Marketplace permissions for their Zoom Account, must pre-approve the app.
